runs.kind: first execution of the binary-tier signature policy (t24)
runs.verdict: 185/7 on both legs -- all seven reds in t24, and the FIXTURE was the fault

preRegistrationClassification.ruleAsWritten: leg A or B green -> the tier copy is not checking signatures at all; the POLICY is failing and the fix is in lib/preserve.sh, never in t24.
preRegistrationClassification.whyNot: t24.4 went red in the same run: the 'unsigned' tier carried 6 Sig: lines. The fixture copied the victim out of the HOST store, where objects substituted from cache.nixos.org keep that cache's signature in the store database, and nix copy propagates it. The tier was therefore signed by a key trusted BY DEFAULT, so leg A and leg B were accepted for a reason unconnected to the policy and leg C succeeded for a reason unconnected to the key.
preRegistrationClassification.correctClassification: FIXTURE DEFECT -- the section 21 case 't24.3 or t24.4 RED -> that is a fixture problem too'. The classification as written assumed the fixture was what it claimed.

whatIsEstablished.aboutTheSignaturePolicy: NOTHING. Run 30 neither showed that the tier path checks signatures nor that it does not. A green leg A is consistent with both.

testedEnvelope.note: The causal conclusion holds IN THE TESTED CONFIGURATION. It is not a claim that Nix never requires these mechanisms.

status.nextRunPolicy: A further cold run of the same commit yields almost no information. The next run should exist because a new falsifiable claim exists.
status.resultStatement: Within the tested envelope, E1-E3 are confirmed, the claimed necessity of the workarounds is falsified, and removal of those workarounds preserves every pre-registered observable. The experiment protocol itself was prospectively validated, by rejecting a defective measurement criterion BEFORE the intervention.

note: The commit that closed the experimental line. Recorded by a later commit, because a commit cannot name its own hash -- the same measured/recorded split this file exists to keep straight.

status.runIndexPolicy: Only executions that carry an empirical claim are indexed as runs. A documentation commit still triggers CI; that execution is operational verification, not a new experiment, and is deliberately absent from `runs`. Otherwise the index becomes a graveyard of identical green executions where the numbers grow and the knowledge does not.
